n988aea7e355.s: The Non-Cooperation Movement, the first nationwide mass movement, made which body a mass force for the first time?
n988aea7e355.x: Swaraj was not won within one year, but the NCM made the Indian National Congress a mass force for the first time.

ndfaede16a24.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the events of 1921-23?
o: The Prince of Wales boycott (17 November 1921) came before the Bardoli resolution
The Bardoli resolution (11-12 February 1922) came before Gandhi's arrest
The Swaraj Party was formed before the Bardoli resolution
Gandhi was arrested in March 1922, before the Swaraj Party was formed
ndfaede16a24.x: The Swaraj Party was formed in 1923, after the Bardoli resolution (February 1922) and Gandhi's arrest (March 1922).

n71ea7e74320.s: Gandhi supported the Khilafat cause chiefly as an opportunity to forge:
n71ea7e74320.x: Gandhi merged the Khilafat cause with Swaraj and regarded it as an opportunity to forge Hindu-Muslim unity.

new.s: The Khilafat Committee was formed in:
new.x: The Khilafat Committee was organised in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Khalifa.

new.s: At the Karachi Khilafat conference of July 1921, the Ali brothers urged Muslims to quit:
new.x: At Karachi (July 1921) the Ali brothers, Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali, urged Muslims to quit the Army.

new.s: Which Khilafat leader gave up the title 'Haziq-ul-Mulk'?
new.x: Hakim Ajmal Khan gave up the title Haziq-ul-Mulk during the Khilafat-Non-Cooperation phase.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the Khilafat Movement?
new.x: Tej Bahadur Sapru was not a Khilafat leader; he was a mediator of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).

new.s: Who coined the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'?
new.x: Hasrat Mohani coined 'Inquilab Zindabad' and proposed Swaraj as complete independence at Ahmedabad (1921).

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
new.x: The Simon Commission came after the NCM (1920-22), so it could not be a cause; Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh and Khilafat were causes.

new.s: On the day the NCM was launched (1 August 1920), Gandhi returned which medal?
o: Order of the Star of India
new.x: On 1 August 1920 Gandhi returned his Kaiser-i-Hind medal as the NCM began.

new.s: Who presided over the Calcutta special session of the Congress (September 1920) that approved non-cooperation?
new.x: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the Calcutta special session, where Gandhi's resolution passed 1886 to 884.

new.s: Under the constitution adopted at Nagpur (1920), the Congress membership fee was fixed at:
new.x: The Nagpur constitution fixed the membership fee at four annas, not one rupee.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Nagpur session (1920):
1. It set up an AICC of 350 members.
2. It organised Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines.
3. It was presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Nagpur created a 350-member AICC and linguistic PCCs; it was presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar, not Lajpat Rai.

new.s: At the Calcutta special session (1920), Gandhi's non-cooperation resolution was passed by:
new.x: The resolution was carried 1886 to 884; C.R. Das opposed it there.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the NCM programme?
new.x: The programme asked for surrender of titles; retention of titles was not part of it.

new.s: Under the NCM programme, government law courts were to be replaced by:
new.x: The programme called for boycott of law courts and settlement of disputes in panchayat courts.

new.s: Kashi Vidyapith at Varanasi was founded in:
new.x: Kashi Vidyapith, Varanasi, was founded in 1921 during the NCM.

new.s: Besant Theosophical College, Madanapalle, which was NOT an NCM institution, was founded in:
new.x: Annie Besant founded the college at Madanapalle in 1915, before the NCM.

new.s: About how many national schools and colleges came up during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
new.x: About 800 national schools and colleges were started during the NCM.

new.s: Which leader opposed the boycott of schools during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
new.x: Lala Lajpat Rai opposed the boycott of schools, though he presided over the Calcutta special session.

new.s: Saifuddin Kitchlew, who gave up legal practice during the NCM, belonged to:
new.x: Saifuddin Kitchlew of Punjab gave up his practice during the NCM.

new.s: Which of the following did NOT give up legal practice during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
new.x: Prakasam, Rajendra Prasad and Asaf Ali gave up practice; Ambedkar was not among them.

new.s: C.R. Das had earlier defended Aurobindo in the:
new.x: C.R. Das, a Bengal lawyer, had defended Aurobindo in the Alipore Bomb Case.

new.s: The Prince of Wales, whose visit was boycotted during the NCM, landed at Bombay on:
new.x: He landed at Bombay on 17 November 1921, met by a nationwide hartal and clashes in Bombay.

new.s: The Akali movement of 1920-25 was directed against:
new.x: The Akalis sought gurdwara reform against corrupt mahants, leading to the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925.

new.s: The forest satyagraha in Andhra first started in:
new.x: The forest satyagraha first started in Palnadu, led by Kanneganti Hanumanthu.

new.s: The volunteer force 'Ramadandu' was associated with which movement?
new.x: Ramadandu was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya's volunteer force in the Chirala-Perala movement; Shanti Sena belonged to Pedanandipadu.

new.s: Who wrote the song 'Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu'?
new.x: Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu was written by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.

new.s: The banned play 'Viplava Parivarthanam' was written by:
new.x: Viplava Parivarthanam was a banned play by Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri.

new.s: The Rampa Rebellion led by Alluri Sitarama Raju began on:
new.x: The Rampa Rebellion began on 22 August 1922 with a raid on Chintapalli police station.

new.s: After the Congress boycott of the November 1920 elections, the Justice Party won how many of 98 seats in Madras?
new.x: The Justice Party won 63 of 98 seats and formed the first ministry under A. Subbarayalu Reddiar.

new.s: How many people were finally hanged in the Chauri Chaura case?
new.x: The Gorakhpur Sessions Judge sentenced 172 to death, but 19 were finally hanged (1923).

new.s: At Chauri Chaura the crowd was protesting the arrest of its leader while campaigning against:
new.x: The crowd protested the arrest of its leader in the anti-liquor campaign; after police firing it burnt the police station.

new.s: Which leader criticised the withdrawal of the NCM as showing weak leadership?
new.x: M.N. Roy blamed weak leadership; Bose called it a 'national calamity'.

new.s: Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 at:
new.x: Gandhi was arrested at Sabarmati, Ahmedabad, on 10 March 1922.

new.s: Gandhi was charged with sedition in 1922 under which section of the IPC?
new.x: He was charged under Section 124A IPC for three articles in Young India.

new.s: Gandhi's sedition charge of 1922 rested on articles such as 'Tampering with Loyalty' published in:
new.x: The charge was based on three Young India articles, including 'Tampering with Loyalty' and 'Shaking the Manes'.

new.s: At the Great Trial of 1922, Gandhi:
o: Pleaded guilty and asked for the highest penalty
new.x: Gandhi pleaded guilty before Judge Broomfield and asked for the highest penalty; he got 6 years.

new.s: Gandhi, sentenced to six years in 1922, was released in:
new.x: He was released in 1924 on health grounds.

new.s: The Swaraj Party was formed on:
new.x: Announced on 31 December 1922, it was formed on 1 January 1923 as the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party.

new.s: Which Andhra leader formed the People's Party to back the Swarajists?
new.x: The Pithapuram Raja formed the People's Party to back the Swarajists.

new.s: Who was the secretary of the Andhra division of the Home Rule League?
new.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was secretary of the Andhra division and led the opening of its branches.

new.s: In 1917 the Home Rule flag of 5 red and 4 green stripes was hoisted at:
new.x: The Home Rule flag was hoisted at Coimbatore in 1917.

new.s: Who was the first Indian woman President of the INC?
new.x: Sarojini Naidu (1925) was the first Indian woman President; Annie Besant (1917) was the first woman President.

new.s: In January 1921, the APCC meeting at Vijayawada set up Congress committees at the:
new.x: After Nagpur, the APCC met at Vijayawada in January 1921 and set up district, taluk and village committees.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Vijayawada in 1921:
1. The APCC met there in January 1921.
2. The AICC met there in March-April 1921.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the APCC met in January 1921 and the AICC session followed on 31 March - 1 April 1921; they are different meetings.

new.s: The AICC at Vijayawada (1921) set a target of how many charkhas?
new.x: The targets were 1 crore members, Rs 1 crore for the Tilak Swaraj Fund and 20 lakh charkhas.

new.s: The targets set at the Vijayawada AICC (1921) were to be met by:
new.x: The targets of members, funds and charkhas were to be met by 30 June 1921.

new.s: Gandhi's October 1921 tour of Andhra, the peak of the NCM there, covered:
new.x: The October 1921 tour covered Kurnool, Kadapa, Tirupati and Tadipatri; the April tour was coastal.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT visited in Gandhi's April 1921 coastal tour of Andhra?
new.x: Kurnool was covered in the October 1921 tour; Kakinada, Machilipatnam and Rajahmundry were in the April tour.

new.s: The National College of the NCM era in Andhra was at:
new.x: Eluru had the National College, not Tadipatri.

new.s: Pallepadu Ashram of the NCM era was in which district?
new.x: Pallepadu Ashram was in Nellore; Seethanagaram Ashram was near Rajahmundry.

new.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya's Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi was at:
new.x: The Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi of Duggirala was at Chirala.

new.s: The Chirala-Perala, Pedanandipadu and Palnadu episodes of the NCM were all in which old district?
new.x: All three main NCM episodes of Andhra were in the old Guntur district.

new.s: During the Chirala-Perala movement, residents left the town and lived in a camp at:
new.x: Opposing the new municipality and its taxes, residents moved to a camp at Ramnagar.

new.s: The Pedanandipadu campaign of 1921-22 was a refusal to pay:
new.x: Pedanandipadu villages refused land revenue under Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary.

new.s: Under the Forest Act of 1878, the Pullari tax on a cow was:
new.x: Pullari was 12 annas per cow and Rs 1.50 per buffalo.

new.s: In the Palnadu satyagraha, the social boycott of forest officials took place at:
new.x: Officials were socially boycotted at Macherla; the cattle were impounded at Minchalapadu.

new.s: Which Congress leader tried to dilute the Palnadu struggle, preferring social boycott to tax refusal?
new.x: Konda Venkatappayya tried to calm the struggle; Congress preferred social boycott, not tax refusal.

new.s: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was shot dead at Minchalapadu on:
new.x: He was shot dead in the cattle-rescue action at Minchalapadu on 22 February 1922.

new.s: The Delhi AICC that allowed provinces to start civil disobedience including no-tax campaigns met on:
new.x: The Delhi AICC of 5 November 1921 permitted civil disobedience, including no-tax campaigns.

new.s: Who called the suspension of the NCM a 'national tragedy'?
new.x: Subhas Bose called it a 'national tragedy'; Nehru reacted with 'amazement and consternation'.

new.s: Which Andhra leader was given the title 'Andhra Kesari'?
new.x: T. Prakasam was 'Andhra Kesari'; Duggirala was 'Andhra Ratna'.

new.s: The title 'Desoddharaka' belongs to:
new.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was 'Desoddharaka'; Konda Venkatappaiah was 'Desabhakta'.

new.s: Which of the following was a No-Changer after the Non-Cooperation Movement?
new.x: Vallabhbhai Patel was a No-Changer; Vithalbhai Patel, Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das were Swarajists.

new.s: Council work and constructive work together kept the national movement alive during the lull of:
new.x: The two camps proved complementary and kept the movement alive in the 1922-28 lull.

new.s: At the Gaya session (December 1922), C.R. Das's resolution on council entry was:
new.x: C.R. Das, the Gaya president, saw his council-entry resolution defeated, leading to the Swaraj Party.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a founder or member of the Swaraj Party?
new.x: Rajendra Prasad was a No-Changer; Das and Motilal Nehru founded the party and Vithalbhai Patel was a Swarajist.

new.s: Which Congress session allowed the Swarajists to contest the 1923 elections?
new.x: The Delhi special session of September 1923 allowed the Swarajists to contest the elections.

new.s: Who presided over the Kakinada session of the Congress in 1923?
new.x: Maulana Mohammad Ali presided over the Kakinada session (1923).

new.s: Who presided over the Guwahati session of the Congress in 1926?
new.x: S. Srinivasa Iyengar presided at Guwahati (1926).

new.s: Which of the following pairs of Congress session and president is correctly matched?
new.x: Sarojini Naidu presided at Kanpur (1925); Madras 1927 was M.A. Ansari and Gaya 1922 was C.R. Das.

new.s: Vithalbhai Patel was elected President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925 by a vote of:
new.x: He won on 24 August 1925 by 58 to 56 against the government-backed T. Rangachariar.

new.s: The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the result of the Swarajist demand to review:
new.x: Swarajist pressure for a review of the 1919 Act led to the Muddiman Committee.

new.s: The Swarajists split after the death of C.R. Das in:
new.x: C.R. Das died in June 1925 and the party split.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a Responsivist?
new.x: Lajpat Rai, Malaviya and Kelkar were Responsivists; Rajagopalachari was a No-Changer.

new.s: Besides constructive work, the No-Changers favoured:
new.x: The No-Changers focused on constructive work and continued the boycott of councils.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the constructive programme of the 1920s?
new.x: Council entry was the Swarajist strategy; untouchability removal, village panchayats and prohibition were constructive items.

new.s: Who was the secretary of the Andhra branch of the Swaraj Party?
new.x: Unnava Lakshminarayana was secretary; Kaleswara Rao was president and Gadicherla treasurer.

new.s: Ponduru, famed nationally for its khadi, is in which district?
new.x: Ponduru in Srikakulam district was famed nationally for khadi.

new.s: Who was the treasurer of the Andhra branch of the Swaraj Party?
new.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was the treasurer.
